query: What kinds of tickets create heavier agent workload?

per_column.name: resolution_days
per_column.rationale: Time-to-resolution is a genuine constitutive aspect of workload burden -- the temporal/duration component of how much effort a ticket consumes. It is a part-of the burden concept, not merely an external driver.

per_column.name: workload_intensity
per_column.rationale: This is essentially a renamed synonym of the whole concept (workload burden itself) rather than a distinct aspect OF it. It restates the target as a single aggregate score, so it does not carve out a specific non-overlapping facet.

per_column.name: critical_infrastructure
per_column.rationale: Whether a ticket concerns critical infrastructure is an attribute of the ticket that may PREDICT or CAUSE higher burden, but it is not itself a constitutive part of the agent's workload. It is an external driver, not an aspect of the burden.

judge.rationale: Only resolution_days qualifies as a true constitutive facet (the temporal/duration dimension of burden). 'workload_intensity' restates the whole concept rather than decomposing a distinct aspect, and its meaning overlaps with the target itself and with resolution_days, lowering mutual exclusivity. 'critical_infrastructure' is an external predictor/cause, not a part-of facet. As a set, the columns fail to cover the main constitutive aspects of workload burden -- e.g. effort/handling steps, number of reassignments or touches, complexity, communication/interaction volume, and cognitive/priority load are all absent -- so exhaustiveness is low. The decomposition does not satisfy the MECE faceted-decomposition claim.
